findingDetails.title: Five sites still name the cursor Style Reference removed by v0.21.0.0, and one states corner values the checker enforces against
findingDetails.evidence: assets/style-reference/ contains only evilcharts and changelog/v0.21.0.0.md:16 records the cursor removal. Survivors: README.md:48 and scripts/README.md:32 both say --default themes from the cursor bundle (DEFAULT_STYLE_REFERENCE is evilcharts, apply-design-md.cjs:31,150); scripts/apply-design-md.cjs:148 says a cursor capture is carried beside the forms; assets/style-reference/evilcharts/origin.md:3 contrasts itself with a cursor reference beside it; references/template-contract.md:462-464 says the rungs follow the cursor reference at 2px mark, 4px track/swatch/tooltip card, 8px card, while palettes.json radius is 2/4.4/4.4/4.4/8.4 and checkPaletteBlock (:681-696) compares every template block against it. changelog/v0.21.0.0.md:19-21 claims the corner-ladder passage was rewritten to 4.4px/8.4px, so a stated fix did not land.
findingDetails.recommendation: Fix all five sites to name evilcharts and the values in palettes.json, and name the pill rung rather than the tooltip card which reads it.

findingDetails.title: The manual-testing-playbook states twenty-one chart forms where the corpus ships twenty-nine
findingDetails.evidence: Line 50 reads 'The corpus holds twenty-one chart forms across six question families'; assets/templates holds 29 html files and the checker prints 'chart forms under assets/templates: 29'; SKILL.md:137, README.md:32, references/README.md:33, references/template-contract.md:320 and the 29 catalog rows all say twenty-nine; the playbook's own reading-the-chart/headline-agrees-with-the-data.md:101 says 'The twenty-nine forms this scenario reads'. Line 38 of the same playbook promises it does not hand-maintain a count.
findingDetails.recommendation: Correct line 50 to twenty-nine, or remove the number and let the walked tree carry it as line 38 promises.

findingDetails.title: scripts/README.md accounts for 22 of the 42 check families the runner emits and never says the list is partial
findingDetails.evidence: Line 75 names eighteen per-file families; line 97 adds nine more of which six are named and two (legend, tooltip-card) repeat the first list. Thirteen emitted families are named nowhere in the file: cursor-guide, curve-contract, emphasis-budget, finding-cue, mark-policy, metric-block, palette-derivation, ramp-prose, reference-line, source-line, style-reference, table-disclosure, tooltip-indicator. Verified by running node scripts/check-corpus.cjs read-only, extracting the 42 family names it prints and testing each against the document. README.md:124 routes readers here as 'What the corpus validator checks'.
findingDetails.recommendation: Enumerate the remaining families or state that the section names the families the contract discusses while the run prints the full set.

findingDetails.title: The standing proof suite is named in no living packet document
findingDetails.evidence: Neither SKILL.md, README.md, scripts/README.md, references/** nor manual-testing-playbook/** names scripts/tests/ or the command that runs it; grep for 'node --test' over those documents returns nothing. The only living reference is .github/workflows/chart-corpus.yml:35-40, and the remaining path is changelog archaeology (changelog/v0.23.0.0.md:63-64). scripts/README.md:135-422 instead spends about 120 lines on hand-run sed mutations the suite already encodes, against the packet's own doctrine at scripts/README.md:338-339.
findingDetails.recommendation: Name the suite and its command in README.md section 6 VERIFICATION and in scripts/README.md, and mark the manual recipes as the historical record they now are.
